title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its dots AI agents can buy things for users

kept.claim: OpenAI launched/began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet on Friday, November 13, 2026 (not later).
kept.evidence: [0] OpenAI's announcement post is dated November 13, 2026 and begins 'We're introducing ChatGPT Wallet'. [1] TechCrunch, dated Nov 13, 2026: 'On Friday, OpenAI launched a new wallet feature'. [2] 9to5Mac, dated Nov 13 2026, embeds an @ChatGPT post dated November 13, 2026 saying Wallet is 'rolling out starting today to dots'.

kept.claim: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's dots agents complete purchases on the user's behalf.
kept.evidence: [0] available through dots, agents pay. [1] 'lets its agents, called dots, help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf'. [2] headline and body: enables dot agents to make purchases. [3] allows AI agents to complete purchases on behalf of users.

kept.claim: Agents pay without access to the user's actual card details.
kept.evidence: [0] 'first wallet that lets agents pay without access to users' actual card details'. [1] card details 'aren't shared with either the dot or the merchant'. [2] same OpenAI wording quoted. [3] 'without accessing their actual card details'.

kept.claim: OpenAI describes it as the first wallet that lets agents pay without access to actual card details and requires a security check for every purchase. This is OpenAI's own 'first' claim and is not independently verified.
kept.evidence: [0] 'It's the first wallet that lets agents pay without access to users' actual card details and requires a security check for every purchase'. [2] quotes the same sentence, attributed to OpenAI.

kept.claim: The user reviews the items, total and selected card before each purchase and approves it with a security check.
kept.evidence: [1] users 'review the items, the total, and the payment card' before checkout and approve with a security check. [2] 'Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card'. [3] same flow before each transaction.

kept.claim: The security check is a biometric such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan, and each approval creates a record of the purchase the user authorized.
kept.evidence: [1] 'a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint... creates a record'. [2] 'Face ID or a fingerprint scan... clear record'. [3] 'Face ID or a fingerprint scan... a record of what the user authorised'.

kept.claim: Payment uses a payment token (a substitute for the real card number, security code and expiry) and the selected card is charged.
kept.evidence: [1] 'charges the selected card using a payment token, which is a substitute for the user's actual card details'. [2] the payment network provides a payment token; the card is charged. [3] same.

kept.claim: Users add their card once; they do not re-enter payment details for each purchase.
kept.evidence: [1] 'This setup is a one-time thing'. [3] 'Users add a card once and then approve each purchase without re-entering payment details'.

kept.claim: Initial availability: through dots, for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US.
kept.evidence: [0] 'initially be available through dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US'. [1] 'initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers'. [2] 'only available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers... in the United States'. [3] 'initially for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US'.

kept.claim: Eligible users must be aged 18 or older.
kept.evidence: [1] 'ages 18 and up'. [2] '18 or older'. [3] 'aged 18 and older'.

kept.claim: The launch is limited, so OpenAI can learn from real-world use and improve compatibility and reliability with businesses, banks and payment networks before expanding.
kept.evidence: [1] 'limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature'. [2] quotes OpenAI: 'We're starting with limited availability to ChatGPT Pro users'. [3] 'limited rollout will allow it to learn from real-world use'.

kept.claim: Users keep existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes.
kept.evidence: [0] 'preserving existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes'. [1] rewards still earned, dispute protections kept. [2] same OpenAI sentence quoted. [3] 'Users retain existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes'.

kept.claim: The wallet is designed to work with existing commerce infrastructure; existing checkout pages should work without a Wallet-specific integration.
kept.evidence: [0] 'Existing checkout pages should work without a Wallet-specific integration'. [3] 'The wallet's tokens work with existing checkout flows'.

kept.claim: OpenAI advises merchants to allow verified ChatGPT cloud-browser requests using Web Bot Auth.
kept.evidence: [0] 'Allowing verified ChatGPT cloud-browser requests using Web Bot Auth'. [3] recommends configuring CDNs or firewalls to recognise signed requests using Web Bot Auth.

kept.claim: Businesses can build plugins that let agents handle product discovery, availability, carts and checkout. [0] calls these MCP-based. [3] mentions plugins and WebMCP tools.
kept.evidence: [0] 'Building MCP-based plugins for product discovery, availability, carts, and checkout'. [3] 'plugins that let agents check availability or manage carts, or add WebMCP tools'.

kept.claim: OpenAI released a Commerce Partner Playbook and other tools and guidance to help businesses support customers using agents.
kept.evidence: [0] 'we're releasing tools and guidance to help businesses support customers using agents' and links the Commerce Partner Playbook. [1] OpenAI 'published a Commerce Partner Playbook'. [3] 'has published a Commerce Partner Playbook'.

kept.claim: Sites that block AI agents are a limit: Wallet purchases may fail on them.
kept.evidence: [1] retailers are 'blocking AI agents from using their site'. [2] 'The feature won't work with websites that block agents'. [3] some sites and payment systems 'may unintentionally block purchases'.

kept.claim: OpenAI plans to let users set spending limits, purchase categories or time periods and pre-approve purchases, so agents can act more autonomously. This is a future plan, not available now.
kept.evidence: [1] plans to allow users to 'set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods'. [3] same parameters, with pre-approved purchases and biometric safeguards.

dropped.claim: The Paypers article is dated 16 Nov 2026, three days after the Nov 13 launch. The launch is not a Nov 16 event.
dropped.evidence: [3] byline date '16 Nov 2026'. The articles from [0], [1] and [2] are dated Nov 13.

dropped.claim: The wallet was built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. The full OpenAI page could not be fetched; a search snippet of it appears to list Chase as well, but I could not read it, so that is unconfirmed.
dropped.evidence: [0] 'Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa'. [2] 'includes a partnership with American Express, MasterCard, and Visa'. [3] 'Developed in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa'.

dropped.claim: Eligible cards are US-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express.
dropped.evidence: [1] 'with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express'. [3] says only 'eligible US-issued cards'.

dropped.claim: Amazon is the largest retailer banning AI agents. Single source.
dropped.evidence: [1] 'the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon'.

dropped.claim: For American Express, this is the first integration of its Agentic Commerce Experiences. Single source.
dropped.evidence: [3] 'the wallet is the first integration of its Agentic Commerce Experiences'.

dropped.claim: OpenAI is working with fraud providers Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd, and payment service providers Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe, to recognise legitimate agent transactions. Single source.
Merchants keep control of customer relationships, pricing, fulfilment, returns and customer service. Single source.
dropped.evidence: [3] 'merchants keep control over customer relationships, pricing, fulfilment, returns, and customer service'.
